title: Characterize critical legacy booking workflows

input.requestedOutcome: Add and publish repeatable characterization tests for LAM-77 without changing production behavior.
acceptanceCriteria: Document booking persistence, edit-preserve fields, cancelled-status aggregates, seat locks, boat assignment, and rate-type pricing.
Document intentional exceptions before modular extraction.
Do not modify production behavior, persistence, schema, root configuration, ADRs, or SYSTEM_MAP.md.
constraints: Base the isolated task branch on origin/main.
Use only Node built-ins and test-owned globals; do not install dependencies or change shared configuration.
Create a PR but do not merge it or transition Jira.
assumptions: The monolithic HTML is the behavior source under characterization.
The repository's Node 18+ engine supports node:test and vm.

output.summary: Added eight isolated Node characterization tests plus an intentional-exceptions fixture for critical legacy booking workflows.

filesChanged.purpose: Extract selected production functions into a test-owned VM context.
Exercise persistence, aggregate, lock, boat, rate, and edit-preserve behavior.
Record intentional compatibility exceptions for future extraction.
Record task inputs, observable output, verification, risks, and rollback.

behaviorChanges.before: Critical behavior was only represented by the monolithic implementation.
behaviorChanges.after: Eight executable tests pin selected current behavior without changing the implementation.

behaviorChanges.before: Existing behavior and data paths were unchanged.
behaviorChanges.after: Existing behavior and data paths remain unchanged; tests use in-memory test doubles.

details: Tests read the legacy HTML source and use an in-memory localStorage double.
No production persistence, API, schema, or migration behavior changed.

decisions: Extract individual named functions instead of executing the entire legacy application.
Select the second save declaration explicitly because the first is the cloud-sync helper and the second is the localStorage persistence implementation.
risks: The extraction harness intentionally depends on named function declarations and selected source structure; a rename or conversion may require test-harness migration.
followUps: Move the cases to module-level tests as corresponding legacy modules are extracted.
Retain fixture exceptions until a separately approved behavior change replaces them.
rollback: Revert the LAM-77 commit; no production code or persisted data is affected.
